papers.title: VS-Suite: Automated Consensus Virtual Screening Platform for Improved Screening of Small Molecules
papers.abstract: Growing the recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine leaning (AI&ML) approaches accelerated small molecules screening against targeted proteins with limited computational resources and time. Finding accurate binding pose and affinity prediction is challenges task and traditional docking tools and lacks the reproducibility. Development of the Co-folding model is paradigm shift in drug discovery and development, allowing to predict protein ligand complexes without experimental crystal structures. Notably Boltz-2 predicts the complex structure along with binding affinity directly using protein FASTA sequence and ligand SMILES. Our previous studies confirmed that Boltz-2 is classify binder non-binders effectively. Autodock Vina and GNINA are widely used docking with knowledge and CNN based scoring functions allows to screen potential small molecules. We developed in-house VS-suite (Virtual Screening Suite) multi-environment conda orchestration designed to automate the docking workflow only using FASTA and SMILES string as inputs via streamlit-based browser GUI which integrates the boltz-2 for the complex structure prediction followed docking using AutoDock Vina for Gnina. Validation on 58 antiviral nucleoside analogues screened against SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro). VS-Suite is available at https://github.com/Vsubuchem-lab/Virtual-screening-suite-VS-Suite. This consensus approaches helpful in rapid screening of small molecules against selected targets. The findings and VS-suite support its utility as a rapid and reliable tool for hit identification and rational drug development.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses of lysine isonicotinylation-related gene expression in diabetic foot ulcer healing
papers.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers have heterogeneous healing outcomes. We integrated public single-cell and bulk RNA-sequencing datasets to identify cell-type-specific lysine isonicotinylation (Kinic)-related transcriptional patterns and exploratory candidates associated with healing. The atlas comprised 56,568 cells across 14 cell types, with Kinic-related signature scores differing by cell type and healing group. Intersecting bulk differentially expressed genes, single-cell high-versus-low-score differentially expressed genes, and coexpression module genes prioritized LDHB, ISG15, and HAUS1 as exploratory candidates. Seven subtypes were identified among healing-enriched fibroblasts. ISG15-associated enrichment highlighted interferon and inflammatory responses. Simulated deletion of each candidate reduced mean similarity to a non-Healer reference state. Docking identified LDHB ZINC250K 0191530 as the lowest-scoring evaluated pair, while a single 100-ns simulation showed displacement of the ligand from its initial pose. These analyses prioritize LDHB, ISG15, and HAUS1 as exploratory candidates and characterize their cellular context in diabetic foot ulcer healing. Their expression patterns within healing-enriched fibroblasts provide clues to the cellular and molecular differences associated with healing outcomes.

papers.title: Input Construction Accounts for Most PoseBusters Clash Failures on RNA-Ligand Complexes
papers.abstract: PoseBusters, a widely used test of the physical validity of ligand poses, was calibrated on protein-ligand crystal structures, and whether its checks transfer to RNA has not been measured. Applied without filtering the input to 2,970 deposited RNA-ligand poses, the receptor-clash check failed 527 of 2,931 (18.0%), and all but 7 of the failures were in covalently bonded nucleotides or in entries that contain protein, were solved by cryo-electron microscopy or were resolved at worse than 2.0 [A], so most failures are associated with which structures and ligand records entered the input set. On a high-resolution set constructed after these failures were attributed, the check failed 3 of 149 (2.01%; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.00-4.58%) against 0.32% for the protein benchmark, a difference this set cannot resolve, and the PoseBusters calibration rule selected a threshold of 0.735 against the shipped 0.75. We give a seven-step dataset construction protocol and a tool, rnaprep, that implements its first four steps. On 139 redocking targets, with accuracy measured in the crystal frame without superposition, requiring a valid pose cost NucleoDock 25.2 points (69.06% to 43.88% within 2 [A]) and AutoDock Vina none, and cut the lead of NucleoDock from 38.9 points (95% CI 26.5-50.0) to 13.7 points, a lead not clearly distinguishable from zero (95% CI 1.3-27.5; cluster permutation P = 0.053). For these two programs in one redocking regime, the result supports reporting validity alongside RMSD in RNA docking benchmarks.

papers.title: Distance-stratified benchmarking of variant-effect predictors on β-lactamase deep mutational scanning data
papers.abstract: Mutations far from the active site of antibiotic-resistance enzymes can change resistance, but it is unclear what information predicts their effects. We asked how the performance of a protein language model (ESM2), a structure-based stability predictor (ThermoMPNN) and simple structural descriptors changes with distance from the catalytic residues, using deep mutational scanning data for the {beta}-lactamases TEM-1 (four assays) and VIM-2 (one assay). We measured Spearman correlation and AUROC within distance bins, with bootstrap intervals over positions. In TEM-1, ESM2 accuracy fell with distance (Stiffler assay: {rho} = 0.72 below 8 [A] and 0.42 beyond 20 [A]), while the stability score rose ({rho} = 0.41 to 0.70). Adding stability to a model of ESM2, solvent accessibility and neighbour count improved cross-validated {rho} by 0.02 below 8 [A] and 0.10 beyond 20 [A], and the combined model did not decline with distance. The pattern held across binning schemes, in a continuous-distance model, and when any one of five contiguous distal stretches was removed. Two TEM-1 assays are nearly duplicates, and the Deng assay was too noisy to be informative. VIM-2 has only seven positions beyond 20 [A] and showed no detectable trend within 20 [A], so it neither supports nor contradicts the TEM-1 pattern. Nine distal TEM-1 positions remained more sensitive than the models predicted. In TEM-1, predicted stability was more informative than the language model far from the catalytic site, and the language model was stronger near it. Distance-stratified reporting could add to variant-effect benchmarks. The study is exploratory and uses one structure and one phenotype per assay.

papers.title: Standard benchmarking inflates gene-prioritization accuracy estimates
papers.abstract: Benchmark results tell clinics which gene-prioritization system to trust and the field what counts as progress. Standard benchmarking practice --- testing each system using its latest knowledge databases --- can inflate system accuracy estimates and invite data leakage. We formalize the Fairbench protocol: testing may use only knowledge available strictly before the patient's assessment. Against prepublication snapshots dated by case report, on one public case collection, standard benchmarking inflated Top-1 accuracy by 40.5--80.5 percentage points across Exomiser, LIRICAL, Phrank and Phen2Disease. In every system, over half the tested patients had a causal-gene phenotype association whose only recorded source was their case publication. Reassessing three systems' published benchmarks with reproduced or reconstructed references showed the same direction in all five comparisons. Retesting undiagnosed patients with the latest knowledge database is good care. But benchmark results are read as performance at the patient's assessment, and Fairbench is a necessary data-hygiene condition for that reading.

papers.title: StarCrew: A pipeline for exploratory analysis of Starship cargo
papers.abstract: BackgroundStarships are giant cargo-mobilizing mobile elements within the fungal subphylum Pezizomycotina that harbor diverse gene content, including genes for virulence and heavy metal resistance. Although Starship elements carry a vast array of cargo genes, the overall composition and function of this cargo remain largely uncharacterized for most elements. While existing bioinformatic tools have been designed for the identification of these elements, a gap remains in tools for characterizing their gene content while accounting for its specific characteristics. ResultsTo address the gap in gene content analysis of Starships, we present StarCrew, a bash- based pipeline designed for systematically characterizing the cargo gene diversity and turnover within Starship elements. We demonstrate that StarCrew robustly handles datasets of varying diversity, providing the capacity to cluster elements based on collinear regions, identify nested insertion events, perform element classification, and highlight overrepresented genes within a dataset. Additionally, StarCrew serves as a diagnostic tool to flag elements requiring boundary curation. We found that the accuracy of the pipeline was sensitive to the quality of input gene models and the precision of initial element boundaries delineation. Demonstrating its utility, we identified a putative pseudokinase as a new conserved protein distributed across Starships. ConclusionsStarCrew provides a practical and versatile resource for the continuous exploration of Starship gene content, designed to adapt alongside our expanding understanding of these mobile elements. Finally, we propose a complementary system to group elements with potential shared beneficial traits, based on collinear blocks, called Functional Constellations.

papers.title: CellTouch: Learning to separate touching nuclei in anisotropic 3D cell cultures
papers.abstract: 3D-oids, such as spheroids and organoids, are essential models in drug discovery and precision medicine, and quantitative analysis requires every nucleus to be segmented separately. Accurate 3D instance segmentation remains challenging, because nuclei are densely packed and touching, and volumes are sampled more coarsely along the Z-axis than laterally. Most existing methods were developed for near-isotropic data and tend to merge neighbouring nuclei. To address this challenge, we propose CellTouch, a deep learning method for anisotropic 3D nuclei instance segmentation that predicts flow fields and a contact channel, which separates touching nuclei directly from the network output. Ablations showed that the contact channel is the key design element, and CellTouch outperformed state-of-the-art methods on in-house data and widely used public datasets. Most importantly, dense Z-sampling is not required: CellTouch segmented nuclei as accurately at a 2 um Z-step as at 0.5 um, reducing acquisition time and data volume four-fold.

papers.title: GNEval: A Context-Specific Benchmark for Gene Network Inference with Single-Cell Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Gene network (GN) inference plays a critical role in understanding gene relationships and their roles in biological functions and diseases. Existing single-cell GN inference methods often rely on limited data from individual studies. Single-cell foundation models, pretrained on large and diverse datasets, provide a range of gene-gene association signals that offer a promising basis for GN inference. However, it remains unclear which GN properties these signals capture and how they compare with domain-specific methods. To address this gap, we introduce GNEval, a unified benchmark for evaluating pretrained model derived gene associations for network inference. We benchmark 21 gene representations and association scores from 11 models, including static gene embeddings (S), contextual embeddings (C), and gene-gene attention scores (A). GNEval assesses inferred networks based on their consistency with functional and perturbational evidence, including 14 Perturb-seq datasets across diverse cell systems, perturbation types and data sizes. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity across evaluation tasks and models. Rankings based on Gene Ontology and Perturb-seq evidence were nearly uncorrelated (Spearman {rho} = -0.05). Context-independent representations showed a substantial advantage in recovering functional relationships ({Delta}AUROC = 0.13), whereas context-dependent gene associations improved recovery of perturbation-associated differential expression relationships by 3.8x. The domain-specific method achieves relatively strong performance on both evidence types, offering a better balance across the two evaluations than most foundation-model-derived networks. Overall, gene representations and association scores show task-specific strengths, highlighting the need for task-aware selection and integration with domain-specific methods.

papers.title: Task-aligned foundation model representations enable single-cell cytokine response inference
papers.abstract: Inferring cellular responses from single-cell transcriptomes requires interpreting changes relative to an appropriate baseline while retaining cell-type context. Here we present CYTAP, which adapts frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings for cytokine-response inference by combining donor-adjusted receiver states with deviations from matched control centroids. CYTAP uses a shared classifier to assign relative single-cell response scores across 90 cytokines and supports unpaired analyses using counterfactual control references. Baseline-relative representations improved held-out-donor prediction with both State SE and scFoundation. Across independent perturbation datasets, CYTAP prioritized applied cytokines, including when receptor transcripts were sparsely detected, and ranked administered cytokines among the top ten in both in vivo datasets. In an unpaired COVID-19 cohort, inferred responses were associated with severity, and IL-6 response scores correlated with plasma IL-6 concentrations. These findings support the use of biologically defined references to adapt pretrained representations for functional response inference.

papers.title: EHRMENEIA: A Benchmark for Foundation Models on Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
papers.abstract: Electronic health record foundation models are evaluated using heterogeneous targets, vocabularies, and adaptation procedures, preventing systematic characterization across model families. We introduce EHRMENEIA (https://ehrmeneia.upc.edu/), a benchmark that provides a multidimensional evaluation framework for next-event prediction, multi-horizon event occurrence, trajectory fidelity and few-shot representation transfer. EHRMENEIA preserves each model's native vocabulary and temporal representation while mapping clinical outputs to shared evaluation objects. Applied to two released clinical checkpoints and two synthetic demonstrations, the framework exposed substantial differences not only in performance but in the clinical questions that could be evaluated from each model--dataset interface. EHRMENEIA introduces a view of benchmarking in which the supported clinical evaluation domain is identified before performance within that domain is interpreted. The framework therefore shifts foundation-model benchmarking from scalar ranking toward characterization of what can, and cannot, be inferred from model outputs.

papers.title: A Benchmark for Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Enzyme Kinetic Parameters of Metabolic Networks
papers.abstract: Large-scale kinetic models predict how metabolism responds to genetic and environmental perturbations, but building them at scale is limited by the scarcity of experimentally determined enzyme kinetic parameters. Generative machine learning has been proposed to address this bottleneck, yet prior work has each introduced a single, bespoke architecture, leaving open which generative paradigm suits this problem and why. We introduce a benchmark suite for generative modeling of high-dimensional enzyme kinetic parameter sets: labeled datasets of kinetically feasible Escherichia coli models paired with a mechanistically grounded evaluation harness that scores generated ensembles on dynamical stability and agreement with experimentally observed phenotypes, rather than statistical realism alone. Using it, we compare three standard architectures at matched capacity, a conditional variational autoencoder, a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty, and a RealNVP normalizing flow, each under two conditioning schemes (a discrete high/low label and a continuous, graded key-performance-indicator target), across a difficulty ladder from one mutant phenotype to a stringent class of nine reproduced jointly. Two findings stand out. The architectures trace a consistent concentration-exploration trade-off, the VAE concentrating, the flow exploring and extrapolating, the GAN in between, but this ordering is overturned at high stringency by the conditioning scheme: at the joint class, continuous targets reach 33 to 117-fold enrichment over random sampling for every architecture, whereas discrete labels stay at 1.3 to 15-fold. Beyond the comparison, the suite is an accessible, mechanistically validated reference task for groups outside the kinetic-modeling community to benchmark their own generative algorithms.

papers.title: Thin2Seg: Single-cell Segmentation of Label-free FLIM at Low Photon Counts
papers.abstract: Significance: Fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) of NAD(P)H can measure the metabolism of single cells without labels. However, its weak autofluorescence requires long acquisitions that can lead to phototoxicity, while shorter acquisitions leave too few photons for current cell segmentation methods. This trade-off is aggravated in 3D live-cell models, such as spheroids and organoids, and in thin, highly adherent 2D cultures. Aim: We develop Thin2Seg to adapt a generalist segmentation network to low-photon FLIM using unlabeled recordings and a single annotated training image. The method also assesses which predicted cell masks remain stable under photon loss without additional manual annotations. Approach: We use binomial photon thinning to generate low-photon views of full-photon FLIM recordings. During training, the student network uses these low-photon views to predict the features that a teacher network extracts from the corresponding full-photon images. We evaluate Thin2Seg on macrophage and small intestinal organoid datasets against three approaches: fine-tuning on full-photon images, photon augmentation, and segmentation after denoising. We also use the predicted macrophage masks to pool photons within each cell and estimate fluorescence lifetimes. Results: Thin2Seg achieved the highest mean segmentation F1 scores among the methods tested on both datasets at median budgets of 1 and 0.5 photons per cell pixel. At these budgets, 8-12% of masks accepted by label-free certification failed the overlap criterion against full-photon predictions, compared with 14-48% of masks accepted by Cellpose's flow-error check. At 1 photon per cell pixel, 92% of annotated macrophages were recovered and 53% of lifetimes estimated were within 10% of the full-photon reference. Median cell lifetimes were within 5% of the full-photon values in 95% of macrophage images, and M2a macrophages remained distinguishable from each of the other three polarization states. Conclusions: Thin2Seg enables single-cell segmentation and lifetime analysis of label-free FLIM from much shorter acquisitions. It uses a single annotated training image and segments low-photon FLIM images directly, supporting live-cell analysis at lower photon budgets without a separate image restoration step.

papers.title: Leukocyte content accounts for most microRNA-immune associations in cutaneous melanoma: a confounder-adjusted reassessment
papers.abstract: Loss of antigen presentation allows tumours to escape T cells and resist immune checkpoint blockade. In melanoma cell lines, several microRNAs repress genes of the antigen-presentation machinery, and many microRNAs have been proposed as immune biomarkers in melanoma tissue. Most tissue evidence comes from bulk biopsies, in which both microRNA profiles and immune-gene expression depend on the immune-cell content of the sample. Following a pre-specified analysis plan, we regressed five immune-module scores on 662 mature microRNAs in 431 melanomas from The Cancer Genome Atlas (3,310 tests), with and without adjustment for tumour purity, leukocyte content, interferon tone and clinical covariates. We labelled each microRNA by its likely cell of origin, required target-level evidence for candidates, re-tested nine published microRNA sets, and examined the antigen-presentation programme in four skin-cancer single-cell datasets, three checkpoint-blockade cohorts (155 patients) and survival data. Of 1,334 associations significant before adjustment, 82.5% were lost after it, and 188 emerged only after it. Only 20 of the 127 microRNAs associated with antigen presentation after adjustment were labelled tumour-intrinsic, and none met the target-level criterion. The closest candidate, miR-361-5p (myeloid-suppression module), failed only a multiple-testing correction added after the target-level results were known. Published sets were enriched among unadjusted antigen-presentation associations (odds ratio 3.32) but not among adjusted ones (1.02), and lost significance as often as other microRNAs (83.3% versus 85.8%). In single-cell data, non-malignant cells expressed the antigen-presentation programme more strongly than malignant cells in 19 of 20 contrasts. A higher antigen-presentation score predicted longer survival after adjustment for composition (hazard ratio 0.69) but not for interferon tone (0.86), and the immunotherapy cohorts were uninformative. In melanoma tissue, most microRNA-immune associations reflect the immune-cell content of the biopsy. Showing that microRNAs control antigen presentation in tumour cells will require compartment-resolved measurements and adequately powered target-level tests.

papers.title: Adult gut microbiomes single out individuals at population scale
papers.abstract: Gut microbiome DNA is shared openly under the assumption that only human host DNA poses an ethical risk. Here we show that querying all publicly available metagenomes with one stool sample recovered another sample from the same person for 94% of 483 adults. Extrapolated to the world population, recovery rates remain well above the re-identification risk threshold advised for public release.

papers.title: FunDLM: A Foundation DNA Language Model for Fungi
papers.abstract: Background: Fungi are important pathogens and biotechnology resources, but lack a broadly applicable fungal DNA language model. Models trained on diverse fungal genomes can support functional interpretation of genomic variants and a broad range of genomic tasks. Results: We introduce FunDLM, a family of four DNA language models pre-trained on 426 fungal reference assemblies spanning 217 genera and 14.3 Gb of sequence. Without task-specific training, FunDLM-Medium-1024bp distinguished phenotype-associated missense variants of Saccharomyces cerevisiae from synonymous controls with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.875. It performed comparably to Evo 2, a generalist model with about 15 times more parameters, and better than Nucleotide Transformer v3. The model also recognized mutations that disrupt start codons or introduce premature stop codons in S. cerevisiae and the blast fungus Pyricularia oryzae. Its scores for missense variants, computed from DNA alone, correlated with those of protein language models in S. cerevisiae and two Fusarium species (Pearson correlation 0.57-0.75). After fine-tuning, FunDLM-Small-1024bp identified supernumerary chromosome sequences in four Pyricularia isolates not used for training (average precision 0.884), and FunDLM-Medium-1024bp recognized centromeres on a chromosome withheld from training (AUROC 0.908). Fine-tuned models also predicted three histone modifications in an isolate and on chromosomes not used for training (AUROC 0.910-0.996). Conclusions: FunDLM provides reusable sequence representations for assessing functional impacts of fungal variants as well as annotation of genomic and epigenomic features. The released models, data, code, and benchmarks support applications across fungal species.

papers.title: Reconstructing regulatory histories of cell fate decisions from single-cell lineage and multi-omics
papers.abstract: Understanding how distinct cell identities emerge from common progenitors requires access to regulatory histories that molecular snapshots cannot directly reveal. We introduce RegArch, a probabilistic framework integrating transcriptomic profiles, chromatin-derived evidence, and time-scaled cell lineages to reconstruct terminal and unobserved ancestral gene regulatory networks (GRNs). These lineage-resolved networks enable characterization of regulatory reorganization, prioritization of differentiation-associated and branch-biased regulators, and identification of constitutive, lineage-associated, and state-restricted modules. Simulations demonstrate ancestral network recovery and improved terminal GRN inference. In Caenorhabditis elegans, inferred ancestral GRNs combined with measured regulator expression generated target-expression signatures preferentially matching their corresponding progenitor profiles. EMS lineage analyses identified a shared regulatory module and branch-enriched modules with distinct ancestral representation. In zebrafish hearts sampled after injury, developmental ancestry informed endocardial- and epicardial-associated candidate regulator prioritization. RegArch thus generates testable hypotheses about the regulatory origins of cellular diversity.

papers.title: L++: A Language for Programming Life
papers.abstract: Living systems run on a code written in DNA or RNA, but expressing that code as a model that scientists can write, run and read remains difficult. We present L++, a holistic programming language in which life can be described, simulated and, beyond that, designed; its nouns are biological, and people and AI systems can both write it. Molecules, reactions, compartments, cells, organs and populations are written directly and nest by containment, so one grammar spans a reaction and the population around it. Quantities carry units, objects take places in space, and values can be set in time. Named kinetic parameters select one family of rate laws, from mass action to cooperative enzyme kinetics, and a few operators write complexes, states and gene products in one line. Modules compose by import, and a process can be written by its inputs, outputs and rate before its mechanism is known; the aim is that one description can model an organism or design one. lppc compiles a program and lpps runs it, and a run repeats exactly with the same build, options and seed. Ten programs written with an AI assistant, from an enzyme in a tube to a lake ecosystem and a drug therapy from molecule to patient, show the language across levels of biological organization, and a genome-scale virtual Escherichia coli, reported separately, shows it holds a whole organism. Our ultimate goal is the Human Code: the human, from molecules to the whole body, written in L++ as a mechanistic model that runs.

papers.title: rnaModScan: context-aware deep learning-based filtering of nanopore m6A and inosine calls
papers.abstract: Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS) can detect multiple RNA modifications, but falsepositive background calls complicate transcriptome-wide analysis. We developed rnaModScan,a deep learning filter that integrates Dorado scores for all eight modification types with local sequence, repeat, and per-read alignment features to distinguish N6-methyladenosine (m6A) and inosine candidates from background calls. Using public RNA004 data, we evaluated site classification by grouped five-fold cross-validation and assessed transfer to HeLa cellular RNA using model weights fitted exclusively to HEK293T cellular RNA and unmodified in vitrotranscribed controls. For m6A sites outside the canonical DRACH motif, filtering removed 92.85% of the Dorado/modkit candidates while retaining 93.34% of their original matches to the GLORI reference map. The F1 score relative to DRS-covered GLORI sites increased from 3.04% to 26.76%. For inosine, filtering removed 83.44% of the candidates while preserving 99.86% of their original Slic-seq matches, and the reference-map F1 score increased from 5.22% to 22.05%. Filtering also brought the motif, repeat, and transcript-position distributions of retained candidates closer to those in the orthogonal short-read maps generated by GLORI and Slic-seq. These results support rnaModScan as a practical complement to Dorado-based RNA004 analysis for prioritizing transcriptome-wide m6A and inosine candidates.Availability: rnaModScan is available at https://github.com/uedaLabR/rnaModScan and archived in Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24546829).Keywords: direct RNA sequencing; RNA modifications; Dorado; deep learning; inosine; m6A

papers.title: Pretrained Decision Models in Bioinformatics: Comparable to Active-Learning Screening, Baseline-Dependent in Cell-Type Annotation, Behind a Trained Mass-Spectrometry Re-scorer
papers.abstract: Much of biomedical research rests on small, repeated decisions with a fixed set of answers: whether a study belongs in a systematic review, whether two trial claims contradict each other, which type a cell is, whether a peptide-spectrum match is correct. Pretrained decision models answer such questions without training on the data at hand, but how far they can replace the methods established for each task is unknown. Here we tested two such models, Jev and d3-ultra, against an established tool or, where none exists, published benchmark results. We evaluated four tasks with known answers, ordered from text input to numeric input. On text, the models were usable without any training: in screening for 39 systematic reviews, their reading order showed no detectable difference from the active-learning screener ASReview at the ideal stopping point. In detecting contradictory drug-trial claims, they scored close to the best published model. On gene names, they helped only where a curated marker database was weak: they trailed it in pancreas and led it in heart, by a margin that depended strongly on how the database was applied. On numbers from one mass-spectrometry run they accepted 30 to 55% fewer matches at 1% estimated error than a re-scorer trained on that run. Pretrained decision models are therefore a practical first pass for text-based decisions and worth trying where curated knowledge is thin, but no substitute for a tool trained on the experiments own numbers.

papers.title: Tumor2Line: population-aware tumor-cell line alignment for cancer cell line selection
papers.abstract: Abstract Cancer cell lines are widely used in cancer research and drug development, yet their representativeness of patient tumors varies across models and biological contexts. Here, we introduce Tumor2Line, a population-aware framework that reframes cancer cell-line selection as an alignment problem between tumor and cell-line populations using unbalanced optimal transport. Tumor2Line improved the recovery of documented tumor-cell line pairs over conventional similarity-based approaches. Systematic analysis across 22 cancer lineages revealed that tumor-cell-intrinsic programs were generally better preserved, whereas programs with greater tumor microenvironment dependence showed lower fidelity. Furthermore, Tumor2Line-selected cell lines showed drug-sensitivity patterns associated with clinical treatment outcomes and improved concordance in genetic dependency profiles with patient-derived organoids. These findings provide a basis for more informed selection of cancer cell-line models and help researchers interpret preclinical findings in the context of model-specific representational fidelity. Tumor2Line is available at https://github.com/Duan-Lab1/Tumor2Line Keywords: Cancer cell lines; Tumor-cell line alignment; Population-aware modeling; Cancer model fidelity; Optimal transport

papers.title: StrucMind links protein contacts and ligand environments to atoms in PyMOL
papers.abstract: StrucMind provides two PyMOL plugins for comparing protein contact maps and examining the interactions around a bound ligand. A contact seen in only one structure can reflect a difference in packing or a gap in the coordinates needed for comparison. Contact Maps aligns corresponding residues, identifies retained, gained and lost contacts, and records why a comparison remains unresolved. Structure Analysis measures direct ligand-protein contacts, traces paths through individual water molecules, and characterizes aromatic packing and pocket geometry. Users can select a contact or a water-mediated path to inspect the atoms in PyMOL. Exported atom identities, distances and coordinate coverage let a colleague retrace the assignment. Keywords. Molecular recognition, Noncovalent interactions, Protein contact maps, PyMOL, Water bridges.

papers.title: ComProg resolves spatial cell-cell communication into dynamic communication programs and receiver responses
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics enables cell-resolved inference of ligand-receptor (LR) signaling, but the resulting communication maps are highly redundant, sensitive to LR database choice and difficult to relate to receiver-cell transcriptional responses while accounting for cell identity and spatial context. Here we present ComProg, a framework that organizes spatially inferred cell-cell communication into communication programs representing recurrent combinations of LR pairs and identifies associated transcriptional responses in receiver cells through cell-type- and niche-matched comparisons calibrated against synthetic negative-control genes. We applied ComProg to spatial transcriptomic datasets spanning mouse kidney injury and repair, non-small-cell lung cancer profiled in two and three dimensions, and gastric cancer during immune checkpoint blockade. ComProg identified compact sets of communication programs that tracked injury and repair, localized to distinct tumor compartments, recurred across serial sections and differed between treatment response states. In injured kidney, program-associated transcriptional responses were concentrated in receiver cell types expressing the corresponding receptors, supporting the biological specificity of the inferred associations. Together, ComProg provides a framework for reducing complex LR-level communication maps into interpretable and comparable signaling programs and linking these programs to transcriptional responses in specific receiver-cell populations.

papers.title: Confident but misplaced: a model-free ruler for post-translational modification placement by AI structure predictors
papers.abstract: AI structure predictors accept post-translationally modified (PTM) residues, but whether they place the added atoms where crystallography finds them, and whether their confidence reveals when they do not, is unknown. We first built a ruler from experiment alone: independent crystal structures of the same site reproduce the added atoms of oxidised cysteine and methionine to 0.32 [A], the closest pre-cutoff library rotamer lies at 0.41 [A] and a model-free guess at 4.17 [A]. We then predicted 176 hold-out PTM sites, released after every model's training cut-off, with RareFold, Boltz-2, Chai-1 and AlphaFold 3, using identical inputs and thresholds fixed before measurement. On oxidised Cys/Met (up to 34 sites in 25 proteins), the three all-atom models place the matching distal atoms of neighbouring canonical side chains to 0.35-0.38 [A] but the added oxygens at 1.19-1.51 [A]; 29-41 % of placements are wrong by more than 2 [A], as sterically plausible rotamers that the electron density does not support. RareFold misplaces ordinary side chains as well. Across all PTM classes, residue confidence does not flag the failure: at pLDDT [≥] 90, 24-46 % of modified-residue placements are catastrophic, 3.5-5 times the rate for matched canonical atoms. One seed rarely samples the correct rotamer; more seeds sample it more often, yet the models' own ranking does not select it. Methyllysine shows the same gap, whereas for pyridoxal-lysine the models diverge (AlphaFold 3 1.13 [A], Boltz-2 4.96 [A]). A high residue pLDDT at a modified residue therefore does not verify its side chain.

papers.title: GeneArbiter improves plant genome annotations while preserving established gene models
papers.abstract: As plant genome resources expand, updating established annotations requires incorporating improved gene models without disrupting correct structures or stable identifiers. We developed GeneArbiter, an evidence guided framework that treats annotation updating as a correction preservation problem. GeneArbiter uses the current annotation as a backbone, integrates alternative models with RNA splice junction and homologous protein evidence, and applies constrained language model arbitration followed by deterministic release and identifier reconciliation. In rice MH63, GeneArbiter recovered 4,701 reference loci missed by the current annotation while losing 1,890 current exact loci, yielding a net gain of 2,811 exact matches and increasing the gene level exact hit rate from 70.77% to 77.77%. It retained 97.54% of protein coding genes in the mature TAIR12 annotation and improved protein set quality metrics across 16 plant genomes. Independent transcript and protein evidence further supported GeneArbiter selected structural revisions at reference discordant loci. These results establish GeneArbiter as a conservative and traceable framework for maintaining plant genome annotations as new predictions and biological evidence accumulate.

papers.title: Inferring transcriptional bursting dynamics from scSLAM-seq data
papers.abstract: Transcription is a bursty, stochastic process. How transcriptional regulators reshape bursting dynamics during cellular responses remains poorly understood, largely because most single-cell RNA sequencing experiments measure only steady-state RNA abundance. Here, we present buRst, a probabilistic framework that infers burst frequency, burst size, and RNA degradation rates from metabolically labeled single-cell RNA sequencing (scSLAM-seq) during acute perturbations, without assuming steady state. It jointly models labeling measurements and RNA dynamics, propagating uncertainty from sparse labeling data into kinetic estimates. We applied buRst to acute MYC depletion in two melanoma cell lines. MYC amplified burst size in a manner scaling with its promoter occupancy, whereas it reduced burst frequency genome-wide, independently of occupancy. As a result, only strongly bound genes showed net activation, reconciling models of MYC as a selective activator and as a global amplifier of transcription.

papers.title: HapAdapter: A Transfer Learning Protocol for DNA Foundation Models Adapted to Diploid Personal Epigenomes
papers.abstract: The rapid rise of large language models (LLMs) has spurred the development of genomic language models (gLMs) that capitalize on the key features of natural language present in biological sequences. Moreover, DNA foundation models, a sub-class of gLMs, have demonstrated impressive accuracy in predicting a wide range of functional tracks from DNA sequence input. However, current DNA foundation models are exclusively trained on haploid reference genome sequences -- despite personal and graph genomes becoming the new standard for genomic analyses. This is principally because the cost to train gLMs on a personal diploid genome for a single individual is not currently practical. To help reconcile this disconnect between the current available use-cases of DNA foundation models with the modern direction of genomic sequence analysis, we present HapAdapter, a transfer-learning protocol that builds a small Siamese network on top of any pre-trained foundation model to enable inference from full diploid personal genome context. To demonstrate the utility of this method, we train a set of HapAdapter heads to predict allele-specific effects across assays on two representative foundation model backbones: DNABERT-2 and AlphaGenome. We demonstrate that our lightweight adapter more than doubles DNABERT-2's allele-specific discrimination and triples AlphaGenome's (130% and 210% gain in AUROC above chance, respectively, averaged over nine assays).

papers.title: A Genome-Scale Virtual Escherichia coli in the L++ Language
papers.abstract: A virtual organism is a computational model, mechanistic or learned from data, that predicts how a living system grows, adapts and responds to genetic edits, drugs and environments. As a first step toward such a model, we are building a virtual Escherichia coli, and here we present its first version, E. coli version 1.0, written for K-12 MG1655 in the L++ programming language. The model writes the cell as a biologist reads it, in one cell definition that compiles to 33,246 species and 41,649 reactions over 4,484 gene loci. Every gene's transcription, translation and decay are written out, for 4,196 of the 4,374 transcribed genes with the gene's own nucleotide and residue counts from the genome sequence, so the proteins that give E. coli its identity and functions, from metabolic enzymes to the machinery that replicates, divides and builds the cell, are each made from their own gene, with the promoter constants of 2,016 genes set toward measured protein abundances. The code wires 360 of 377 essential-gene candidates into processes that growth needs, among them all 293 that at least two genome-wide screens call essential; 177 of the 360 are read by gates and slowdowns written from those screens' calls, so for them the model's requirement follows the screens by construction. Twenty-eight two-component systems are written, and on development versions the two built from measured constants, for osmolarity and phosphate, reproduce the direction of their responses and the promoter order their constants were set to give. In a modified rich medium the cell divides every 1,100 to 1,400 s, at a pace set by a replication rate chosen to fit a 20-minute cycle. Of 95 metabolite pools measured in glucose minimal medium, 78 start within tenfold of measurement, 82 lie within it over t=1,000 to 3,000 s and 65 over t=10,000 to 20,000 s, and the model states where it does not yet match, among them 31 pools held at fixed values. Because the organism is code, a deletion, a retuned promoter or an added module is an edit, so one model serves both to understand the cell and to design its variants, and we hope to extend it toward a complete virtual E. coli together with scientists who bring their expertise and measurements.

papers.title: Capturing human expertise for AI-assisted molecular structure annotation
papers.abstract: We developed a large language model-based tool that captures expert reasoning in bile acid structure elucidation, drawing on hand written notebooks, scientific literature, and recorded voice-to-text analytical sessions. It generates human-readable reports detailing evidence for and against candidate structures, tracing each inference to its source and identifying ambiguities. When applied to data, the tool proposes bile acid conjugates lacking reference spectra.

papers.title: Resplitting LIT-PCBA with MolSCISSOR: A Memory-Efficient, Quasi-Deterministic Framework for Reducing Structural and Physicochemical Biases
papers.abstract: Reliable training-test partitioning is essential for developing and evaluating virtual screening (VS) methods, particularly in the era of machine learning (ML). However, existing molecular dataset splitting approaches do not simultaneously address key challenges in rigorous VS evaluation: cross-partition structural bias, test-set inter-class physicochemical bias, high memory requirements, limited scalability, stochastic allocation, a lack of automated optimization and of flexible training-test similarity control. We introduce MolSCISSOR, a lightweight, memory-efficient, quasi-deterministic framework for stratified data partitioning that integrates clustering and training-test allocation through multi-objective optimization. MolSCISSOR is used to repartition LIT-PCBA, a well-established VS benchmark comprising 15 target-specific datasets of experimentally confirmed actives and inactives, exhibiting substantial class imbalance, many of which are large-scale. We show that simple baseline ML models achieve significantly above-chance screening performance on the original AVE-derived partitions, indicating residual biases. The MolSCISSOR-generated benchmark, SPLIT-PCBA, is more challenging than both the AVE variant and that obtained using a BitBIRCH-Lean clustering-based workflow, with stricter cross-partition structural separation and improved physicochemical balance between test-set actives and inactives. MolSCISSOR mitigates stochastic variability, requires less memory than AVE, Lo-Hi and DataSAIL, and supports multiple split configurations with varying cross-partition similarity. MolSCISSOR and SPLIT-PCBA are freely available at https://github.com/caominhtr/molscissor and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23942580.

papers.title: AUTOENCODIX: powering a hub for biological representation learning models
papers.abstract: Autoencoders are a foundational architecture for biological representation learning and empower methods for denoising, multi-modal integration, explainable embeddings, and synthetic data generation. But, new architectures are scattered across isolated repositories, which hampers benchmarking, the reuse of pretrained models, and the transfer to new data modalities. Here, we present the next generation of AUTOENCODIX, a Python package and model hub for biological representation learning. Its modular, standardized API unifies preprocessing, training, hyperparameter optimization, evaluation, generation, and explanation across a growing set of architectures, now including disentangled, masked, semi-supervised, and 2D/3D image autoencoders. To demonstrate its use at scale, we tuned, trained, and benchmarked 15 large autoencoders on a balanced corpus of 3.7 million human cells from CELLxGENE, including nine ontology-based variational autoencoders whose latent dimensions represent core cellular functions and were defined by three large language models (LLMs). The biological-informed embeddings performed on par with classical Principal Component Analysis in downstream classification while being explainable by design, and in synthetic data generation they produced more biologically plausible error profiles than conventional variational autoencoders. Finally, AUTOENCODIX offers a new and unique combination of three pillars of explainability: by-design with biologically-informed latent dimensions, post-hoc gene-to-latent attribution scoring, and LLM-based knowledge integration for verbal description and hypothesis generation. AUTOENCODIX is open-source, open for community extensions and all pretrained models are available via Hugging Face for application on other single-cell gene expression data.
